en: The Philippines consists of exactly 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the old count of 7,107.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo lowered its peak elevation by approximately 260 meters.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground navigable waterway that flows directly into the sea.
The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, extending approximately 540 kilometers along eastern Luzon.
Baguio City has an average annual temperature of 18 degrees Celsius, making it the coolest major Philippine city.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, plunging to a maximum depth of 10,540 meters.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering a total land area of approximately 109,965 square kilometers.
The San Juanico Bridge connects Samar and Leyte, spanning exactly 2.16 kilometers across the San Juanico Strait.
Mount Hamiguitan hosts a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only one to two meters tall.
